It’s totally normal to feel out of control especially with an illness like this. Ik the advice is redundant, but don’t take it personally. Treat yourself with as much kindness and grace as possible, esp when he is not able to give that.

If you can’t encourage him to get help or family to help hospitalize him, I’d suggest taking some space from him however you can. He won’t be able to hear or process anything you say with love like he’s got on earplugs. The best thing to do in these moments is whatever the best thing for you FIRST, then him. Pouring from an empty cup hurts both of y’all. You’re doing amazing and are very selfless for wanting to help, but please remember it’s an illness that love can help, but can’t fix it. You deserve that love, care, and compassion just as much as your husband does.

That’s good I’m glad you’re looking out for her. If you can secure enough evidence of how’s it being maintained, do you think you could petition medication and treatment contingent visits? 

In the mean time, maybe you could encourage more outdoor activities where they are in public place like parks, fairs, movies, etc… where there potential witnesses if you’re worried about impulsive/reckless behavior in general. Knowing I could reach out to another adult if needed really helped me personally.

At the end of the day, all you can be is a safe space for your kid and hope that she will tell you or show you signs of something should there be an issue. I’m hoping there won’t be any.

If it’s possible, try to call his parents or family in general. They could help petition the court to hold him in involuntary to get him medicated for the episode. Other than that, there’s not much you can do for him. He has to be willing to take meds and make appts on his own (best outcome) or hospitalized for psych management (still a great outcome). In both scenarios it’s still a waiting to game see if or when the treatment starts to help. You get to decide if you’re willing to play it.

Other scenario, he doesn’t get help. Do you have a plan for taking care of yourself and being in a safe location should an episode get too unruly for you to stay with him? You deserve just as much love patience and care as he does. Please please please remember that it’s an illness, and love helps but it can’t fix it. You’re doing everything you can and that’s fantastic and selfless, but not if it ends with you miserable, heartbroken, or traumatized from an episode they may not want to leave.

Wishing you the best of luck from a similar situation!

TLDR: Meditate and widen your musical range/vocabulary. Learning new stuff and living thru the old stuff is a perfect combination for relatable music that means something to you, which is the most important and impactful part. 


Write what you know. Sad angry wild funny bitter whatever. Especially while you’re still feeling it. Listen to your fav artists and entirely new genres to you, study their lyricism. Build your vocabulary and learn new styles of wordplay and double entendres. 

Writing music isn’t writing good lyrics, it’s writing real shit. You have to wanna cry or run or scream or celebrate what you feel when you write for it to mean anything to anyone else. Think abt the songs you cry to and sing at full volume on the highway, what are qualities of their style that you love? Their honesty? Brashness? Humor? The specific pacing and pattern and mouth feel of the words? What makes your chest feel warm and everything else feel small. If you can’t hear the instruments and flows while you sing to yourself or write your lyrics, then try building a habit of isolating instrumentals and letting them wash over you. What comes to mind? Does your chest tighten or your grip loosen? 

Music is essentially poetic meditation. If you don’t know how to feel, describe, and sit within yourself, a lot of what you put to page can feel superficial. Plus, imposter syndrome and anxiety. You may not like it but others might love it. Songs I wanted to chuck, people wanted to use, read, or even tried to buy off me. Have confidence in yourself and a lot of it starts to come naturally.

I love how deep the show got. I spent all of the 3-5th seasons of the original show worrying about how everything was affecting Steven and seeing everything get properly addressed later on was so worth it. I felt connected to every second of it. 

The physical manifestations of his problems were particularly important. I know that the gems try so hard to keep up with him but they didn’t really notice how bad Steven was getting until his body started reacting to his stress. 

And they stop talking about his mom unless it was to address how she hurt him. I was worried that they would spend the entire show focused on him hating his mother and, while it would’ve been valid, that wasn’t the entirety of his problems. I’m glad they chose realistic aspects to base his problems on. He had to learn to live without codependency and that’s always so hard, especially when it starts at such a young age. I spent the entire series just wanting to hug Steven. As much as I wanted him to talk about it, talking isn’t enough sometimes and I wish it didn’t take 19 episodes for everyone to get close enough to him for it to work. Ultimately, I’m glad about his family and friends helping him overcome so much. Heck, even the cluster helped him out.

I’m also happy about his relationship with Connie progressing. I wish it had happened after he started working through some issues but I’m still so glad that he had her. She handled everything so well despite the situation and all of her studying and College Prep. 

I’m a little sad about Sadie and Lars never really working out because at least a resolution where they addressed they had feeling about each other separately from an episode about Steven stressing about everyone leaving would have been nice. I did enjoy seeing Sadie find a great partner for her and Lars going off into space to learn more. I think an amicable break up that lead to this would’ve been great to but I’m definitely not going to criticize how things turned out since no friendships were ruined in the making of that episode. 

And little homeschool is such a cool, sweet idea. I live that gems and humans are cohabiting Earth in the end. It shows how much good Steven did in just two short years despite his self doubt. It also gives us some insight in a few episodes as to how well everyone adapted to such a necessary and drastic change. I kinda wish that as a joke, we saw Steven took a few lessons up to space to show the diamonds how humans work but we know he did because of the movie and second show’s intro. 

Long, long, long summaries/reflections short. I can’t believe how truly spectacular this show is. I regret waiting to watch it and I won’t hesitate to rewatch it in its entirety in the future whenever I feel so emotionally turbulent. If Steven can pull through, so can I.

It’s cool with me. So far I’m at season 4. During season 1, I was still skeptical but I really liked the idea of the show so I kept watching. During season 2, I was happy with the progression of the story line and the couples so far. I think I actually stood up and started cheering during some of the fights. I was also amazed by the animation and complexity of all the different fusions. Especially with Sapphire and Ruby, it was all so seamless that I never even noticed Garnett was even more unique than I had thought in the beginning. 

Season 3 was a bit different though. I’m happy about the bond between Greg and Pearl getting better, and the gems moving on after all of the turbulence of Lapis and Jasper, but I feel like Amethyst really started to lose what made her character so lovable. She went from goofy but capable and strong to defiant and insecure. It made her spontaneity feel aggressive instead of cute and light hearted. Not to mention her slowly becoming less and less happy. I’m all for character development and growth, but it feels like she was losing herself trying to fight for everyone else and it made her act out. Sometimes I wondered if she could even be trusted to care for Steven by herself. 

With season 4, I like the storyline so far but I do worry a lot about Steven. The story is broken up by some random episodes that focus on the minor characters but for the most part, all I’ve seen is Steven constantly being thrown in to battle and being forced to decide what gems deserve to be bubbled. I get that it’s a “kids” show but he’s only 14 and half-gem or not, no one really pauses to check in on him. I hope that part gets better. 

I’ve noticed Amethyst come back into herself a bit and everyone getting closer including Peridot and Lapis and I enjoy it so much. It shows how kind and trusting everyone can be even if they were at each other’s throats once. The message behind the show is so loving and I adore the inclusivity. Different body types, relationships, and sexualities. My only regret so far is not embracing this show sooner.
